title: Deployment circuit-breaker and customer escalation runway
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Problem: Recent model rollouts have produced intermittent semantic regressions in hosted customers and divergent behavior between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments due to differing kernel selection and KV cache priming. The absence of a fast, unilateral stop mechanism that can be applied consistently across environments delays mitigation and complicates customer communications.

Goal: Implement a deployment 'circuit-breaker' service and accompanying operational runway (alerts, playbooks, customer comms templates) that allows SRE/Eng to safely stop a rollout (per-model, per-region, per-customer-tier), triage the regression, and either rollback or hotpatch within a documented SLA window. The solution must work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and preserve data residency and tenant isolation constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Circuit-breaker API that can pause traffic for a model variant at the route level and return 429 with standard retry headers
Rollback orchestration that can be triggered from circuit-breaker and will perform KV cache reconciliation or safe cache flush when needed
Unified alerting rule across Hosted/Dedicated/Private that surfaces regression signal (latency + quality composite) into PagerDuty with tenant context
Customer-facing escalation templates (initial notification, status updates, resolution) for high-impact customers
Runbook with decision matrix: rollback vs hotpatch vs pin-by-customer, including SLA windows and who-does-what
End-to-end test harness that simulates canary failure and validates circuit-breaker behavior in staging
work_items: Design circuit-breaker data model and policy engine (per-model, per-region, per-tenant rules)
Implement control-plane API and CLI for triggering pause/unpause operations
Wire circuit-breaker events into rollout controller and routing layer
Add hooks to Dedicated control plane agent for on-prem signals and safe pause acknowledgement
KV cache reconciliation tool: validate and optionally flush affected worker caches during rollback
Add dashboard: active circuit-breakers, paused rollouts, impacted tenants and SLOs
Author customer communication templates and handover checklist for CSMs

risks: Private deployments may have network controls that prevent immediate pause acknowledgement; we need a fallback offline marker and operator workflow
Aggressive cache flush during rollback can cause transient latency spikes and increased token costs for affected tenants
Overuse of global pause could impact many customers; policy granularity must be per-customer and per-route
Customer trust risk if communications are slow or inconsistent across channels (console + email + CSM)
qa_notes: Create a synthetic canary job that intentionally injects a semantic regression to validate pause -> rollback path
Verify Dedicated agent respects pause marker when offline and exposes a manual override for on-prem ops
Confirm 429 responses include Retry-After and a standardized JSON body with incident id
